subject: ACME POC: integration plan and success criteria
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: integration plan and success criteria

Hi Marissa  thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can finalize the trial timeline: 

Summary of our goals
- Evaluate Redwood for customer-facing chat summarization and knowledge retrieval (internal KB).
- Key success criteria: 1) summary quality (precision/recall on a 50-sample test set), 2) latency p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms, 3) cost parity vs current prototype (target <= 60% of current per-conversation token cost), 4) stable streaming for partial responses so our UI can render as the model generates.

Integration scope
- We'll integrate via API calls from our backend (Node service) and evaluate streaming + tool-calling to fetch facts from our KB.
- We expect to run 2-week trial with a 3-week extension possible for deeper load testing.

Questions / asks for Redwood
1) Can you send a one-page POC plan with owners, week-by-week milestones, and the technical integration checklist (SDKs, sample endpoints, streaming, tool calling examples)?
2) Any constraints on test data handling / retention during the POC? Need confirmation for our security team (SOC2 evidence).
3) Can you estimate token cost for our expected volume (we'll share sample traffic soon)?

Proposed next steps
- If we get the plan today, we can sync engineering and book a 60-minute runbook session Friday.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Director, Product  ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC: integration plan and success criteria

Hi Sarah  great to meet you and Kyle today, appreciate the clear goals. See attached a concise POC checklist and a sample code bundle (Python/Node)  attaching: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf, redwood-api-sample-code.zip. Below is the high-level plan and the immediate owners.

POC owner & contacts
- Commercial/coordination: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.com)
- Technical lead (Redwood): Rishi Malhotra, Solutions (rishi@redwood.com)
- SE/Integration support: Vivek Kulkarni (vivek@redwood.com)

High-level POC plan (2 weeks standard)
Week 0 (prep, completed before kickoff)
- NDA & MSA check (legal)  done
- Technical access: API key + temp staging org created by Redwood (we'll send creds via your SSO admin)
- Test data handoff: ACME provides 50 sample documents and a sample traffic trace

Week 1 (integration & baseline)
- Day 1: Kickoff + runbook (60m)  introduce engineers and define success metric thresholds
- Day 23: Integration: install SDK, implement /v1/generate for summarization endpoints, implement streaming client for partial response rendering
- Day 45: Implement tool-calling flow: Redwood function calling + your KB lookup endpoint; sample code in attached zip
- Deliverable: working end-to-end demo on staging, baseline quality run on the 50-sample set

Week 2 (evaluation & load)
- Day 68: Run evaluation harness (we provide a small script) to collect quality metrics; iterate on prompts and tool config
- Day 910: Load test to target throughput (we recommend starting at 5 RPS, scale to 10 RPS for p95 validation)
- Deliverable: metrics report + recommendation (pass/fail vs success criteria)

Success criteria (draft)
- Summary quality: F1 >= 0.78 on ACME 50-sample test (we'll help compute)
- Latency: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms for 1k token average requests in staging
- Streaming: <200ms partial token latency (observed in staging)
- Cost: Estimated per-conversation token cost <= 60% of current prototype

Technical integration notes (quick)
- SDKs: Python (pip install redwood-sdk), Node (npm i @redwood/inference) with examples in attached bundle
- Auth: API Key (bearer) or mTLS if your security team prefers; we will provision a staging key with restricted scope
- Endpoints: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate (non-streaming), GET/POST w/ Upgrade websocket for streaming at wss://stream.redwood.com/v1/stream or HTTP streaming chunked responses.
- Tool calling/structured output: use the /v1/generate with "tool_calls": ["kb_lookup"] and include a tools manifest; examples in sample code show calls to your KB endpoint and how to surface them in the UI.
- Rate limits: staging org default 20 RPS, can be increased for load test with short notice
- Logging & audit: We provide request/response logs for the POC as part of the staging org; data retention set to 30 days by default for POC orgs.

Security/compliance
- We are SOC2 Type II compliant; we will provide the standard evidence bundle and a POC-specific checklist (attached). For production/private deployments we can discuss VPC/private options.

Next steps
- I'll share the staging org credentials in a separate secure channel and drop the Drive link with the sample harness. Can we book the engineering runbook Friday 11 Jun at 10:00am PT?

Thanks  sending over the Drive link and checklist now.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC: integration plan and success criteria

Thanks Marissa  this looks good. A couple of clarifying items from our eng lead: 
1) Streaming: are you doing server-sent events (chunked HTTP) or a WebSocket for the low-latency partial tokens? We need to know which approach to wire up on our frontend (we currently support SSE).
2) Tool calling: when you say "tools manifest" can you share the exact JSON schema? We need to know how to map our KB lookup API (auth, expected input/output).
3) Data handling: you mentioned 30-day retention in staging. Can you confirm logs and payloads are not used for model training and that we can opt to redact PII on ingest? Our security team will need the exact wording for the SOC2 assessment.

If you can respond quickly we can confirm the runbook on Friday.

 Kyle
Principal Engineer, ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@acme.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC: integration plan and success criteria

Kyle  great questions. Quick answers inline below, and Rishi/Vivek will be on the runbook to go deeper Friday.

On Thu, Jun 11, 2026 at 08:22, Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@acme.com> wrote:
> 1) Streaming: are you doing server-sent events (chunked HTTP) or a WebSocket for the low-latency partial tokens? We need to know which approach to wire up on our frontend (we currently support SSE).

We support both. For easiest integration with your frontend SSE support, use our HTTP chunked streaming endpoint (POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate with Accept: text/event-stream). WebSocket (wss://stream.redwood.com/v1/stream) is available for bi-directional flows and when you need lower round-trip tooling. Examples: see sample code in attached zip (node/sse-client.js).

> 2) Tool calling: when you say "tools manifest" can you share the exact JSON schema? We need to know how to map our KB lookup API (auth, expected input/output).

Attached sample manifest (tools/manifest.json) in the code bundle  short summary: each tool entry = {"id","name","description","input_schema","output_schema","auth_type"}. For KB lookup you can set auth_type: "bearer" and Redwood will forward the tool call as a signed request to your endpoint. We'll review the manifest on the runbook and help map fields.

> 3) Data handling: you mentioned 30-day retention in staging. Can you confirm logs and payloads are not used for model training and that we can opt to redact PII on ingest? Our security team will need the exact wording for the SOC2 assessment.

Confirmed: POC staging orgs are configured with non-training mode  request/response logs are retained for 30 days for debugging and are not used for model training. We also support pre-ingest redact rules (either client-side or via Redwood transform) to strip PII; we'll provide the redact rules template. Rishi will share the SOC2 evidence snippet and the exact policy during the runbook.

I'll schedule the runbook for Fri 11 Jun 10:00am PT and send a calendar invite now (invite sent). Looking forward to the session  Rishi and Vivek will be there to walk through the manifest, SDK install, and a short live integration.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
